decision.rationale: At the pre-registered n=3000 stratified sample, the physically relevant noise grid (sigma in {1e-3, 5e-3, 1e-2} p.u.) produced essentially step-invariant rho-margin distributions across all three candidate steps, while finer grids primarily reduced the discretisation floor and modestly increased margin saturation at each step's own discretisation sigma (61.4% > 10 nat at 0.1, 62.6% at 0.05, 65.7% at 0.025). The mu(L) curve also contains genuine regulator-tap discontinuities (63 circuit-wide boundaries, jumps up to 1.4e-2 p.u. -- tap_discontinuities.json), making the original 1e-3 p.u. interpolation criterion unattainable by grid refinement and inappropriate as the selection criterion. Step 0.05 therefore provides an intermediate numerical floor (5.145e-3 p.u. discretisation sigma) without the additional saturation of 0.025, at no additional cost (table already built, 70,142 solves, 0 non-converged, 0 NaN).
decision.not_selected_on: interpolation fidelity alone (see tap_discontinuities.json for why that criterion is unreachable here)

rgrid_correction.problem: S1.5 (the decisive load-axis test) failed on the original 15-pt log R grid: L* within 1 grid step = 38.4% on the full 28875-event training split, need >90%. Root cause (not a bug): the corpus training resistances {0.1,1,10} Ohm were deliberately kept off-grid (see the pre-correction R_GRID comment, preserved in git history), which let the joint profiled argmin over (tau,R,L) trade a nearby-but-wrong R against a compensating L shift, out-fitting the true (off-grid) point. R* itself still landed within 1 step 99.7% of the time -- only L* was corrupted.

remedies_compared.dense25 (spec S1.7 branch-on-failure rem: FAILED: L* within 1 step = 58.6% overall (52.4%/32.2%/91.0% at R=0.1/1/10) -- still far below 90%. Pure density does not remove the R-L compensation mechanism.

rgrid_correction.cost_of_the_fix: S1.7 argmin_R-at-corpus-R sub-test is now much less informative at the three values that matter: r_star_exact_frac rises 64.8% -> 95.2%, partly by construction (R_true can now literally equal a grid point), not from improved operator fidelity. Not fully vacuous (95.2%, not 100%). Any future S1.7 R-interpolation claim should use off-corpus R values, not {0.1,1,10}.
rgrid_correction.not_redone: S1.2 l_step=0.05 was re-checked (not re-decided) on 2026-09-25 against the corrected table: results/pcstgnn/operator/lgrid_post_rgrid_fix/lgrid_summary.json. Interpolation error per L step is essentially unchanged (confirms the R-grid fix does not touch L-axis smoothness); the step-invariance and saturation-ordering pattern S1.2 selected on is preserved (0.05 still sits in the middle). l_step=0.05 stands. Unexpected finding: PSM top-1 accuracy at each step's own discretisation sigma jumped 0.555/0.556/0.562 -> 0.865/0.904/0.942 for steps 0.1/0.05/0.025 -- the R-L compensation the S1.5 fix removed was also corrupting location attribution, not just L recovery. See results/pcstgnn/operator/S1.5_RGRID_CORRECTION.md.
